title: Check that grafted taxa and missing clades respect their grafting constraints — check_grafting_constraints
code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  # List the missing taxa to graft missing_taxa_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),   # Items are named after Taxon_name (same names, same order)   Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5", X4 = c("t26", "t18")),   Excluded_subclades = list(X1 = list(c("t10", "t19")), X2 = NULL, X3 = NULL, X4 = NULL))  # --- Perform grafting of missing taxa--- #  # Graft the missing taxa with graft_missing_taxa() grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                   verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # --- Check one grafted phylogenies --- #  # Check that the grafted taxa respect their constraints, and that the backbone is preserved check_results <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_phy, phy_backbone = phy,                                             missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list) #> 4 taxa checked #>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0 #>   - Target clade violated:          0 #>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0 #>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.82e-09 (9.65e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06) #>   => All constraints respected # Inspect results check_results #>     map simulation seed Taxon_name in_tree include_target_clade_stem #> X1 <NA>          1 1234         X1    TRUE                      TRUE #> X2 <NA>          1 1234         X2    TRUE                      TRUE #> X3 <NA>          1 1234         X3    TRUE                      TRUE #> X4 <NA>          1 1234         X4    TRUE                      TRUE #>    target_position target_ok excluded_ok n_excluded_violated excluded_violated #> X1           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #> X2           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #> X3      tip_branch      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #> X4           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #>    states_ok ranges_ok   ok #> X1        NA        NA TRUE #> X2        NA        NA TRUE #> X3        NA        NA TRUE #> X4        NA        NA TRUE # Check overall results attr(check_results, "all_ok") #> [1] TRUE  # --- Check several grafted phylogenies --- #  # Build 3 grafted phylognies (i.e., simulations) with the same backbone and constraints grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                    nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Check all resulting grafted phylogenies at once check_results_multi <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_phys, phy_backbone = phy,                                                   missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list) #> 3 phylogenies checked (no map), 4 taxa each #>   - Phylogenies respecting all the constraints: 3/3 #>   Violations, over all the phylogenies (number of taxa x phylogenies): #>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0 #>   - Target clade violated:          0 #>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0 #>   - Backbone: preserved in 3/3 phylogenies, branch lengths shifted by max 9.65e-11 of backbone depth (tolerance = 1e-06) #>   => All constraints respected  # With several simulations: the data.frame has the columns 'map', 'simulation' and 'seed', # and the summary is printed once for all the phylogenies head(check_results_multi[, c("map", "simulation", "seed", "Taxon_name", "ok")]) #>    map simulation      seed Taxon_name   ok #> 1 <NA>          1      1234         X1 TRUE #> 2 <NA>          1      1234         X2 TRUE #> 3 <NA>          1      1234         X3 TRUE #> 4 <NA>          1      1234         X4 TRUE #> 5 <NA>          2 488349520         X1 TRUE #> 6 <NA>          2 488349520         X2 TRUE  # An additional attribute provide a summary per phylogeny: # number of taxa that failed, backbone preserved, all constraints respected attr(check_results_multi, "phylogenies") #>    map simulation      seed n_failed backbone_preserved all_ok #> 1 <NA>          1      1234        0               TRUE   TRUE #> 2 <NA>          2 488349520        0               TRUE   TRUE #> 3 <NA>          3 469344150        0               TRUE   TRUE   # --- Check missing clades grafted with graft_missing_clades() --- #  # With a 'Sister_clade' item, the missing clades are checked (one row per missing clade)  # Prepare a missing_taxa_list for missing clades missing_clades_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3"),   Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t26", "t18"), M2 = c("t26", "t18"), M3 = "t5"))  # Graft the missing clades with graft_missing_clades() grafted_clades <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                        verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Check results check_clades <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_clades, phy_backbone = phy,                                            missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list) #> 2 missing clades (3 taxa) checked #>   - Missing from the grafted tree:        0 #>   - Not forming one clade:                0 #>   - Not sister to their sister clade:     0 #>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.82e-09 (9.65e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06) #>   => All constraints respected # Inspect results check_clades[, c("missing_clade", "Taxon_names", "monophyletic", "sister_position", "ok")] #>   missing_clade Taxon_names monophyletic sister_position   ok #> 1             1      M1, M2         TRUE            stem TRUE #> 2             2          M3         TRUE      tip_branch TRUE   # --- Check the constraints from several traits, with biogeographic ranges --- #  # With the stochastic maps of several traits used to assign grafting constraints, # 'allowed_states' has one element per trait, # and 'treat_states_as_ranges' is a logical vector with one value per trait # used to identify which trait was treated as biogeographic ranges.  # Load datasets data(toy_backbone) data(toy_simmap_ranges) data(toy_simmap_elevation) data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation)  # Graft phylogeny using elevation and biogeographic ranges as constraints grafted_phy_traits <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,     missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation,     simmap = list(biogeo = toy_simmap_ranges, elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),     allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), NULL),     treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE),     verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # The result has the joint columns 'states_ok' and 'ranges_ok' (ranges of the 'range trait'), # and the column 'states_ok_<trait>' for each trait. The summary details the failures per trait. check_traits <- check_grafting_constraints(     phy_grafted = grafted_phy_traits,     phy_backbone = toy_backbone,     missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation,     allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), NULL),     treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE)) #> 7 taxa checked #>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0 #>   - Target clade violated:          0 #>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0 #>   - Allowed states violated:        0 (biogeo: 0, elevation: 0) #>   - Range not in graft-point state: 0 #>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.53e-09 (9.06e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06) #>   => All constraints respected check_traits[, c("Taxon_name", "states_ok", "states_ok_biogeo", "states_ok_elevation",                  "ranges_ok", "ok")] #>         Taxon_name states_ok states_ok_biogeo states_ok_elevation ranges_ok #> New_sp1    New_sp1      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #> New_sp2    New_sp2      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #> New_sp3    New_sp3      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #> New_sp4    New_sp4      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #> New_sp5    New_sp5      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #> New_sp6    New_sp6      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #> New_sp7    New_sp7      TRUE             TRUE                TRUE      TRUE #>           ok #> New_sp1 TRUE #> New_sp2 TRUE #> New_sp3 TRUE #> New_sp4 TRUE #> New_sp5 TRUE #> New_sp6 TRUE #> New_sp7 TRUE  # --- Check both types of missing lineages grafted in one run --- #  # With list(taxa, clades), both parts are checked on the same phylogenies both_list <- list(   taxa = missing_taxa_list,   clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = "t5")))  grafted_both <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list,                                               verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  checks_both <- check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_both, phy_backbone = phy,                                           missing_taxa_list = both_list, verbose = FALSE) names(checks_both) #> [1] "taxa"   "clades" attr(checks_both, "all_ok") # "all_ok" is TRUE if both types of missing lineages are ok #> [1] TRUE

title: Check the feasibility of a grafting plan before grafting — check_grafting_plan
code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny and associated list of missing taxa set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  missing_taxa_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3"),   Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5"))  # --- Check the grafting plan for taxonomic constraints --- #  # Check the grafting plan a priori to detect any issue at low cost plan <- check_grafting_plan(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list, min_tips = 5) #> Grafting plan: 3 taxa #>   - Can be grafted: 3/3 #>   - Target clades smaller than 'min_tips' = 5 (birth-death model fitted on an enclosing clade): 1/3; enclosing clades of 13 tips in the backbone; in practice, the clade used can be nested within them, as previously grafted taxa count towards 'min_tips' #>   => All can be grafted with these constraints plan #>   Taxon_name Target_clade target_n_tips n_branches window_age enclosing_n_tips #> 1         X1     t26, t18            17         33 50.0000000               17 #> 2         X2      t8, t22            13         25 50.0000000               13 #> 3         X3           t5             1          1  0.6368624               13 #>   enclosing_age feasible cause #> 1      20.03438     TRUE  none #> 2      15.28106     TRUE  none #> 3      15.28106     TRUE  none  # --- Check the grafting plan for attribute-based constraints too --- #  # Add a simmap to restrict grafting to some states Q <- matrix(0.04, 3, 3, dimnames = list(c("A", "B", "C"), c("A", "B", "C"))) diag(Q) <- -0.08 simmap <- phytools::sim.history(phy, Q, anc = "A", message = FALSE)  # Check the grafting plan a priori plan_states <- check_grafting_plan(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                    simmap = simmap, allowed_states = "B") #> Grafting plan: 3 taxa #>   - Can be grafted: 2/3 #>   - Cannot be grafted (1): #>       allowed_states              1 #>       e.g., X3 #>   - Share of the available branches in allowed states (feasible taxa): min 8.1%, median 13.4% #>   - Share of the time window with grafting possible (feasible taxa): min 8.6%, median 19.1% #>   - Below 'min_valid_fraction' = 0.1 (1): X1 #>   - Target clades smaller than 'min_tips' = 5 (birth-death model fitted on an enclosing clade): 1/3; enclosing clades of 13 tips in the backbone; in practice, the clade used can be nested within them, as previously grafted taxa count towards 'min_tips' #>   => Some cannot be grafted with these constraints (see the table) # Inspect availability of branches in the allowed states plan_states[, c("Taxon_name", "states_available", "valid_fraction", "time_coverage", "feasible")] #>   Taxon_name states_available valid_fraction time_coverage feasible #> 1         X1          A, B, C     0.08115666    0.08617336     TRUE #> 2         X2          A, B, C     0.18601114    0.29636500     TRUE #> 3         X3                C     0.00000000    0.00000000    FALSE  # --- Check both types of missing lineages at once --- #  # With list(taxa, clades), each part is planned on the same backbone: the output is a named list both_list <- list(   taxa = missing_taxa_list,   clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = "t5"))) plans <- check_grafting_plan(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list, verbose = FALSE) names(plans) #> [1] "taxa"   "clades" # "all_feasible" is TRUE if both types of missing lineages are feasible attr(plans, "all_feasible") #> [1] TRUE

code: # Load the backbone phylogeny data(toy_backbone)  # Plot it with the node IDs ape::plot.phylo(toy_backbone, cex = 0.7, no.margin = TRUE) ape::nodelabels(cex = 0.6, frame = "none", col = "blue")   # A 'missing_taxa_list' with clades defined by node IDs, tips, or both my_missing_taxa_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3"),   Target_clade = list(X1 = 34, X2 = c("t5", "t12"), X3 = "t26"),   Excluded_subclades = list(X1 = list(group_1 = 50), X2 = NULL, X3 = NULL))  # Convert the node IDs into tips tips_missing_taxa_list <- convert_nodes_to_tips(my_missing_taxa_list, phy = toy_backbone) #> 2 node ID(s) converted into tips (a tip node gives its tip, an internal node gives one pair of tips with this MRCA node): #>   - node 34 (internal node, 9 tips) -> t8, t7   [Target_clade: X1] #>   - node 50 (internal node, 3 tips) -> t13, t27   [Excluded_subclades: X1] str(tips_missing_taxa_list, 2) #> List of 3 #>  $ Taxon_name        : chr [1:3] "X1" "X2" "X3" #>  $ Target_clade      :List of 3 #>   ..$ X1: chr [1:2] "t8" "t7" #>   ..$ X2: chr [1:2] "t5" "t12" #>   ..$ X3: chr "t26" #>  $ Excluded_subclades:List of 3 #>   ..$ X1:List of 1 #>   ..$ X2: NULL #>   ..$ X3: NULL  # The total richness of the clades can be converted too total_richness_per_clades <- list(Target_clade = list(32, c("t5", "t12")),                                   total_richness = c(25, 8)) converted <- convert_nodes_to_tips(my_missing_taxa_list, phy = toy_backbone,                                    total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades) #> 3 node ID(s) converted into tips (a tip node gives its tip, an internal node gives one pair of tips with this MRCA node): #>   - node 34 (internal node, 9 tips) -> t8, t7   [Target_clade: X1] #>   - node 50 (internal node, 3 tips) -> t13, t27   [Excluded_subclades: X1] #>   - node 32 (internal node, 17 tips) -> t26, t10   [total_richness_per_clades$Target_clade: clade 1] converted$total_richness_per_clades #> $Target_clade #> $Target_clade[[1]] #> [1] "t26" "t10" #>  #> $Target_clade[[2]] #> [1] "t5"  "t12" #>  #>  #> $total_richness #> [1] 25  8 #>   # Node 34 is the same clade in both objects, and is defined by the same tips converted$missing_taxa_list$Target_clade$X1 #> [1] "t8" "t7" # An already converted list can be used: # the node IDs of the total richness are matched to the tips in the list converted_again <- convert_nodes_to_tips(converted$missing_taxa_list, phy = toy_backbone,                                          total_richness_per_clades = list(Target_clade = list(34),                                                                           total_richness = 14)) #> 1 node ID(s) converted into tips (a tip node gives its tip, an internal node gives one pair of tips with this MRCA node): #>   - node 34 (internal node, 9 tips) -> t8, t7 (tips already used in the list)   [total_richness_per_clades$Target_clade: clade 1] converted_again$total_richness_per_clades$Target_clade #> [[1]] #> [1] "t8" "t7" #>   # --- Convert nodes ID for both types of missing lineages --- #  # With list(taxa, clades), both parts are converted at once, with a shared record of the clades both_list <- list(   taxa = my_missing_taxa_list,   clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = 34, M2 = "t26")))  converted_both <- convert_nodes_to_tips(both_list, phy = toy_backbone) #> 2 node ID(s) converted into tips (a tip node gives its tip, an internal node gives one pair of tips with this MRCA node): #>   - node 34 (internal node, 9 tips) -> t8, t7   [Target_clade: X1 | Sister_clade: M1] #>   - node 50 (internal node, 3 tips) -> t13, t27   [Excluded_subclades: X1] names(converted_both) #> [1] "taxa"   "clades"  # Node 34 is defined by the same tips in the target clade of X1 and the sister clade of M1 converted_both$taxa$Target_clade$X1 #> [1] "t8" "t7" converted_both$clades$Sister_clade$M1 #> [1] "t8" "t7"

Convert continuous values into the same states used in the converted simmap # The output is a list with the states of each value my_states <- convert_values_to_states(missing_values, simmap = my_simmap) my_states #> $Taxon_1 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_2 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_3 #> [1] "medium" #>   # To get a character vector with a single state per value, use unlist() (if tolerance = 0) unlist(my_states) #>  Taxon_1  Taxon_2  Taxon_3  #>    "low"    "low" "medium"   # Same conversion with the cut points and states given directly convert_values_to_states(missing_values, breaks = attr(my_simmap, "breaks"),                          states = c("low", "medium", "high")) #> $Taxon_1 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_2 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_3 #> [1] "medium" #>   # --- Account for the uncertainty of the values with a tolerance --- #  # Taxon_2 has a value just above the second cut point, between the states "medium" and "high" close_values <- c(Taxon_1 = -2, Taxon_2 = attr(my_simmap, "breaks")[2] + 0.1, Taxon_3 = 3) convert_values_to_states(close_values, simmap = my_simmap) #> $Taxon_1 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_2 #> [1] "high" #>  #> $Taxon_3 #> [1] "medium" #>   # With a tolerance of 0.3 trait units, values close to a cut point get several states allowed_states <- convert_values_to_states(close_values, simmap = my_simmap, tolerance = 0.3) allowed_states #> $Taxon_1 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_2 #> [1] "medium" "high"   #>  #> $Taxon_3 #> [1] "medium" #>   # One tolerance per taxon, e.g., the measurement error of each value # (no tolerance for Taxon_1 and Taxon_3) convert_values_to_states(close_values, simmap = my_simmap, tolerance = c(0, 0.3, 0)) #> $Taxon_1 #> [1] "low" #>  #> $Taxon_2 #> [1] "medium" "high"   #>  #> $Taxon_3 #> [1] "medium" #>   # The output can be used directly as the 'allowed_states' of a list of missing taxa missing_taxa_list <- list(Taxon_name = names(close_values),                           Target_clade = list(Taxon_1 = "t1",                                               Taxon_2 = c("t1", "t2"),                                               Taxon_3 = "t1")) missing_taxa_list$allowed_states <- allowed_states

text: Maël Doré

title: Extract the richness and sampling fraction of clades from grafted phylogenies — extract_sampling_info
code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  # Two nested clades: B is nested within A clade_A <- c("t26", "t18") # 17 backbone species clade_B <- c("t26", "t3")  # 9 backbone species, nested within A  # List the missing taxa to graft: 3 taxa in clade A and 1 taxon in clade B missing_taxa_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),   Target_clade = list(X1 = clade_A, X2 = clade_A, X3 = clade_A, X4 = clade_B),   # Optional names of the clades (one per taxon): they must match those of total_richness_per_clades   Target_clade_name = c("clade_A", "clade_A", "clade_A", "clade_B"))  # Total richness of the target clades # NA = unknown richness (i.e., no unsampled species beyond nested clades) total_richness_per_clades <- list(   Target_clade = list(clade_A, clade_B),   Target_clade_name = c("clade_A", "clade_B"),   total_richness = c(25, 12))  # --- Graft the taxa (several simulations) --- #  grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                    total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades,                                    nb_simulations = 5, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # --- Extract the sampling information --- #  sampling_info <- extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_phys,                                        total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades) sampling_info[, c("simulation", "Clade_name", "nb_backbone_species", "nb_grafted_species",                   "nb_unsampled_species", "sampling_fraction")] #>    simulation Clade_name nb_backbone_species nb_grafted_species #> 1           1    clade_A                  17                  4 #> 2           1    clade_B                   9                  3 #> 3           2    clade_A                  17                  4 #> 4           2    clade_B                   9                  1 #> 5           3    clade_A                  17                  4 #> 6           3    clade_B                   9                  2 #> 7           4    clade_A                  17                  4 #> 8           4    clade_B                   9                  1 #> 9           5    clade_A                  17                  4 #> 10          5    clade_B                   9                  3 #>    nb_unsampled_species sampling_fraction #> 1                     4         0.8400000 #> 2                     0         1.0000000 #> 3                     4         0.8400000 #> 4                     2         0.8333333 #> 5                     4         0.8400000 #> 6                     1         0.9166667 #> 7                     4         0.8400000 #> 8                     2         0.8333333 #> 9                     4         0.8400000 #> 10                    0         1.0000000  # The sampling fraction of clade B varies among simulations: # the taxa assigned to clade A can be grafted within clade B (nested in A, so they count for B) # or in A outside of B. As such, the richness of B differs between grafted phylogenies, # while all the taxa are always in A (constant sampling fraction). tapply(X = sampling_info$sampling_fraction,        INDEX = list(sampling_info$Clade_name, sampling_info$simulation),        FUN = mean) #>            1         2         3         4    5 #> clade_A 0.84 0.8400000 0.8400000 0.8400000 0.84 #> clade_B 1.00 0.8333333 0.9166667 0.8333333 1.00  # --- Both types of missing lineages, grafted in one run --- #  # With graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(), the totals of both types are provided as list(taxa, clades) both_list <- list(   taxa = missing_taxa_list,   clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"), Sister_clade = list(M1 = clade_B, M2 = "t5"))) both_richness <- list(   taxa = total_richness_per_clades,   clades = list(Sister_clade = list(clade_B, "t5"), total_richness = c(12, 4)))  grafted_both <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = both_list,                                               total_richness_per_clades = both_richness,                                               nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Output: a named list with the table of each type sampling_both <- extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_both,                                        total_richness_per_clades = both_richness) names(sampling_both) #> [1] "taxa"   "clades" sampling_both$clades[, c("simulation", "Clade_tips", "nb_grafted_species", "sampling_fraction")] #>   simulation Clade_tips nb_grafted_species sampling_fraction #> 1          1    t26, t3                  3         1.0000000 #> 2          1         t5                  0         0.2500000 #> 3          2    t26, t3                  1         0.8333333 #> 4          2         t5                  0         0.2500000 #> 5          3    t26, t3                  2         0.9166667 #> 6          3         t5                  0         0.2500000

backbone phylogeny, with a set of 3 stochastic maps of a trait tip_states <- phytools::getStates(toy_simmap, type = "tips") had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE) if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE) set.seed(118) toy_multiSimmap <- phytools::make.simmap(toy_backbone, tip_states, Graft with the 3 maps and 2 simulations per map as constraints: # the output is a list with one element per map hosting 2 simulations each. grafted_list <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,                               missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states,                               simmap = toy_multiSimmap, allowed_states = c("blue", "green"), "failed")='data.frame':	0 obs. of  2 variables: #>  $ map_2:Class "multiPhylo" #> List of 2 #>   ..$ map_2_sim_1:List of 7 #>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr "cladewise" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "seed")= int 1234 #>   .. ..- attr(*, "map")= chr "map_2" #>   ..$ map_2_sim_2:List of 7 #>   .. ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "phylo" #>   .. ..- attr(*, "order")= chr title: Graft missing clades on a time-calibrated phylogeny — graft_missing_clades
text: Maël Doré

title: Graft missing clades on a time-calibrated phylogeny — graft_missing_clades
code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  # List the missing taxa to graft missing_clades_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4"),   # Sister_clade is named after Taxon_name (same names, same order)   # M1 and M2 share the same sister clade: they are grafted together as one missing clade   Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"), M2 = c("t8", "t22"), M3 = c("t26", "t18"), M4 = "t5"))  # --- Perform grafting --- #  # Graft the missing clades grafted_phy <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                     verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) plot(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)   # Highlight the grafted tips and branches in red plot_grafted(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)    # --- Produce several grafted phylogenies --- #  # The grafting is stochastic: several simulations can be run at once from the same backbone and list # (a "multiPhylo" named sim_1, sim_2, ...; sim_1 is the same as a single run with the same seed) grafted_phys <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                       nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) names(grafted_phys) #> [1] "sim_1" "sim_2" "sim_3" # Seeds of the simulations, to reproduce each phylogeny alone attr(grafted_phys, "seeds") #>     sim_1     sim_2     sim_3  #>      1234 488349520 469344150   # Plot phylos old_par <- par()["mfrow"] par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 1, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #1") # sim_1 plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 2, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #2") # sim_2 plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 3, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #3") # sim_3  par(old_par)   # --- Account for unsampled species --- #  # Account for unsampled species with the total richness of the sister clades. # All the unique sister clades must be listed (NA = unknown richness) total_richness_per_clades <- list(   Sister_clade = list(c("t8", "t22"), c("t26", "t18"), "t5"),   total_richness = c(20, NA, 3)) grafted_phy_richness <- graft_missing_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                              total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades,                                              verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Inspect the resulting clade richness and sampling fractions extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_phy_richness,                       total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades) #>    map simulation seed Clade_tips total_richness total_richness_provided #> 1 <NA>          1 1234    t8, t22             20                    TRUE #> 2 <NA>          1 1234   t26, t18             17                   FALSE #> 3 <NA>          1 1234         t5              3                    TRUE #>   nb_backbone_species nb_grafted_species nb_unsampled_species sampling_fraction #> 1                  13                  1                    6         0.7000000 #> 2                  17                  0                    0         1.0000000 #> 3                   1                  0                    2         0.3333333   # --- Apply attribute-based exclusions --- #  # Restrict the grafting to some states of a stochastic character map (simmap) of the backbone # The toy simmap has three states, "blue", "green" and "red" data(toy_backbone) data(toy_simmap)  # List the missing taxa to graft missing_clades_list <- list(    Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3", "M4", "M5"),    Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t26", "t18"), M2 = c("t26", "t18"), M3 = c("t26", "t18"),                        M4 = "t14", M5 = "t14"))  # The simmap shows that the targeted stem branches recorded state shifts. plot(toy_simmap, col = c("blue" = "dodgerblue", "green" = "limegreen", "red" = "firebrick"))   # We can use 'allowed_states' to limit grafting on the "green" portions of the stem branches    # The stem branch from the "bottom" clade shifts from "green" to "red"    # The terminal (stem) branch of "t14" shift from "green" to "red" too grafted_phy_states <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,                                            missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                            simmap = toy_simmap, allowed_states = "green",                                            verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Plot output phylogeny with colored grafts plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states, use_simmap = FALSE, cex = 0.7)   # The updated simmap is in the output: the new grafted clades branch from the "green" segments # of the stem branches of their sister clades, and each newly grafted clades are entirely "green" # Grafted branches are dashed lines, and grafted tips are labelled in red. plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states,              simmap_colors = c("blue" = "dodgerblue", "green" = "limegreen", "red" = "firebrick"))    # --- Use several stochastic maps (alternative hypotheses of trait evolution) as constraints --- #  # A 'multiSimmap' gives several stochastic maps of the same trait: # the grafting is run with each of them. # Here, 3 maps are simulated from the states of the tips of the toy simmap. tip_states <- phytools::getStates(toy_simmap, type = "tips")  # (the random number generator of the session is restored afterwards) had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE) if (had_seed) old_seed <- get(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv(), inherits = FALSE) set.seed(118) toy_multiSimmap <- phytools::make.simmap(toy_backbone, tip_states,                                          model = "ER", nsim = 3, message = FALSE) if (had_seed) { assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = globalenv()) } else { rm(".Random.seed", envir = globalenv()) }  # Graft using constraints from all 3 simmaps X 2 simulations per simmap grafted_phys_maps <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,                                          missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                          simmap = toy_multiSimmap, allowed_states = "green",                                          nb_simulations = 2, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Inspect output: # A list with one element per simmap, each a multiPhylo with the simulations of the map names(grafted_phys_maps) #> [1] "map_1" "map_2" "map_3" names(grafted_phys_maps$map_2) #> [1] "map_2_sim_1" "map_2_sim_2" # The map and the seed of a phylogeny are included as attributes for reproducibility attr(grafted_phys_maps$map_2[[1]], "map") #> [1] "map_2" attr(grafted_phys_maps$map_2[[1]], "seed") #> [1] 1234   # --- Constraints from several traits at once --- #  # Load the simmap for the second trait: 'toy_simmap_elevation' has two states: "high" and "low". data(toy_simmap_elevation)  # Provide the maps of the traits as a list # The global 'allowed_states' has one element per trait (here, "green" color and "low" elevation). grafted_phy_traits <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,                                            missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,                                            simmap = list(color = toy_simmap,                                                          elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),                                            allowed_states = list("green", "low"),                                            verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # '$simmap' is a list of updated simmaps, one per trait names(grafted_phy_traits$simmap) #> [1] "color"     "elevation"  # Newly grafted clades can only be grafted on and harbor the allowed state in each trait plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 1) # Only 'green'  plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 2) # Only 'low'    # --- Constraints from biogeographic ranges and another trait at once --- #  # One of the traits can be treated as biogeographic ranges: # the allowed ranges do not have to match exactly the range of target stem branch pieces, # any allowed range comprised in a target range is valid (e.g., "A" can be grafted on "AB"). # Here, the first trait holds ranges.  # Load the range simmap data(toy_simmap_ranges)  # The clades are grafted on stem branch pieces in ranges # containing "A" or "B" and in elevation "low" grafted_phy_ranges_traits <- graft_missing_clades(phy = toy_backbone,     missing_taxa_list = missing_clades_list,     simmap = list(biogeo = toy_simmap_ranges, elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),     allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), "low"),     treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE),     verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # '$simmap' is a list of updated simmaps, one per trait: ranges, and elevation names(grafted_phy_ranges_traits$simmap) #> [1] "biogeo"    "elevation"  # Newly grafted clades can only harbor the allowed state/range in each trait # They can be grafted on range that encompasses their allowed range (here, "AB")  # Range: Grafted on "A", "B", or "AB", but inherit only "A" or "B". plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 1)  # Elevation: Only 'low' plot_grafted(grafted_phy_traits, trait = 2)

title: Graft missing taxa on a time-calibrated phylogeny — graft_missing_taxa
code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  # List the missing taxa to graft missing_taxa_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),   # Target clades defined by pairs of tips (MRCA), or by a single tip   # All the other items are named after Taxon_name (same names, same order)   Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5", X4 = c("t26", "t18")),   # Stem of the target clade available for grafting?   # NA uses the global 'include_target_clade_stem' argument (TRUE by default)   # X4 cannot be grafted on the stem   include_target_clade_stem = c(X1 = NA, X2 = NA, X3 = NA, X4 = FALSE),   # Excluded subclades defined by pairs of tips. Only X1 has an excluded subclade   # (the optional name of the excluded subclade, here 'clade_A', is used in messages)   Excluded_subclades = list(X1 = list(clade_A = c("t10", "t19")), X2 = NULL, X3 = NULL, X4 = NULL),   # Stem of the excluded subclades also excluded?   # NA / NULL use the global 'exclude_subclades_stem' argument (TRUE by default).   # Here the stem of the excluded subclade of X1 stays available,   # so X1 can be sister to it, but never nested within it.   exclude_subclades_stem = list(X1 = FALSE, X2 = NULL, X3 = NULL, X4 = NULL))  # --- Perform grafting --- #  # Graft with the default method ("BD_clades") grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                   method = "BD_clades", verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) plot(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)   # Highlight the grafted tips and branches in red plot_grafted(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)   # Graft with the "uniform" method, without using the excluded subclades grafted_phy_uniform <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                           use_excluded_subclades = FALSE,                                           method = "uniform", verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Check that the constraints are respected check_grafting_constraints(phy_grafted = grafted_phy, phy_backbone = phy,                            missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list) #> 4 taxa checked #>   - Missing from the grafted tree: 0 #>   - Target clade violated:          0 #>   - Excluded subclade violated:     0 #>   - Backbone: topology preserved, branch lengths shifted by max 4.82e-09 (9.65e-11 of backbone depth; tolerance = 1e-06) #>   => All constraints respected #>     map simulation seed Taxon_name in_tree include_target_clade_stem #> X1 <NA>          1 1234         X1    TRUE                      TRUE #> X2 <NA>          1 1234         X2    TRUE                      TRUE #> X3 <NA>          1 1234         X3    TRUE                      TRUE #> X4 <NA>          1 1234         X4    TRUE                     FALSE #>    target_position target_ok excluded_ok n_excluded_violated excluded_violated #> X1           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #> X2           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #> X3      tip_branch      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #> X4           crown      TRUE        TRUE                   0                NA #>    states_ok ranges_ok   ok #> X1        NA        NA TRUE #> X2        NA        NA TRUE #> X3        NA        NA TRUE #> X4        NA        NA TRUE   # --- Produce several grafted phylogenies --- #  # The grafting is stochastic: several simulations can be run at once from the same backbone and list # (a "multiPhylo" named sim_1, sim_2, ...; sim_1 is the same as a single run with the same seed) grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                    method = "uniform", nb_simulations = 3,                                    verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) names(grafted_phys) #> [1] "sim_1" "sim_2" "sim_3" # Seeds of the simulations, to reproduce each phylogeny alone attr(grafted_phys, "seeds") #>     sim_1     sim_2     sim_3  #>      1234 488349520 469344150   # Plot phylos old_par <- par()["mfrow"] par(mfrow = c(1, 3)) plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 1, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #1") # sim_1 plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 2, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #2") # sim_2 plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 3, cex = 0.7, main = "Sim #3") # sim_3  par(old_par)   # --- Account for unsampled species --- #  # Account for unsampled species with the total richness of the clades. # All the unique target clades must be listed # (NA = unknown richness, i.e., no unsampled species beyond nested clades) total_richness_per_clades <- list(   Target_clade = list(c("t26", "t18"), c("t8", "t22"), "t5"),   total_richness = c(25, NA, 3)) grafted_phy_richness <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                            total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades,                                            method = "BD_clades", verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Inspect the resulting clade richness and sampling fractions extract_sampling_info(phy_grafted = grafted_phy_richness,                       total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades) #>    map simulation seed Clade_tips total_richness total_richness_provided #> 1 <NA>          1 1234   t26, t18             25                    TRUE #> 2 <NA>          1 1234    t8, t22             16                   FALSE #> 3 <NA>          1 1234         t5              3                    TRUE #>   nb_backbone_species nb_grafted_species nb_unsampled_species sampling_fraction #> 1                  17                  2                    6         0.7600000 #> 2                  13                  2                    1         0.9375000 #> 3                   1                  1                    1         0.6666667   # --- Apply attribute-based exclusions --- #  # Restrict the grafting to some states of a stochastic character map (simmap) of the backbone # The toy simmap has three states, "blue", "green" and "red" data(toy_backbone) data(toy_simmap) data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states)  # This missing_taxa_list has the item 'allowed_states', # with the states where each taxon can be grafted # (NULL for the taxa without a specific value). toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states$allowed_states #> $New_sp1 #> [1] "red" #>  #> $New_sp2 #> NULL #>  #> $New_sp3 #> NULL #>  #> $New_sp4 #> [1] "blue"  "green" #>  #> $New_sp5 #> [1] "green" #>  #> $New_sp6 #> NULL #>  #> $New_sp7 #> [1] "blue" "red"  #>   # Perform grafting informed with the simmap and associated 'allowed_states'. # The taxa without taxon-level states use the global 'allowed_states' argument: # here they can only be grafted on "blue" or "green" sections of the branches grafted_phy_states <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states,    simmap = toy_simmap, allowed_states = c("blue", "green"),    method = "BD_clades", verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Plot output phylogeny with colored grafts plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states, use_simmap = FALSE, cex = 0.7)   # The updated simmap is in the output: # the grafted taxa are in the state of the point where they were grafted. # Grafted branches are dashed lines, and grafted tips are labelled in red. plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states, fsize = 0.5, ftype = "i",              simmap_colors = c("blue" = "dodgerblue", "green" = "limegreen", "red" = "firebrick"))   # States of the grafted taxa: "New_sp1" and "New_sp7" can be "red" # thanks to their taxon-level states, but the taxa using the global states cannot. all_states <- phytools::getStates(grafted_phy_states$simmap, type = "tips") all_states[toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_states$Taxon_name] #> New_sp1 New_sp2 New_sp3 New_sp4 New_sp5 New_sp6 New_sp7  #>   "red"  "blue"  "blue" "green" "green"  "blue"  "blue"    # --- Use several stochastic maps (alternative hypotheses of trait evolution) as constraints --- #  # A 'multiSimmap' gives several stochastic maps of the same trait: # the grafting is run with each of them. # Here, 3 maps are simulated from the states of the tips of the toy simmap. tip_states <- phytools::getStates(toy_simmap, type = "tips")  set.seed(118) toy_multiSimmap <- phytools::make.simmap(toy_backbone, tip_states,                                          model = "ER", nsim = 3, message = FALSE)  # Graft using code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  # The missing taxa and the missing clades are provided together missing_taxa_list <- list(   # Taxa grafted in their target clades   taxa = list(Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3"),               Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"),                                   X2 = c("t8", "t22"),                                   X3 = "t5")),   # Taxa grafted as sister clades. M1 and M2 share the same sister clade: they are grafted together   clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2", "M3"),                 Sister_clade = list(M1 = c("t8", "t22"),                                     M2 = c("t8", "t22"),                                     M3 = c("t26", "t18"))))  # --- Perform grafting of both types of missing lineages at once --- #  # Graft the taxa, then the missing clades, in one call grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                              verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) # All the grafted taxa are identified sum(grafted_phy$grafted_tips) #> [1] 6 plot_grafted(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)   # Graft the missing clades first, then the taxa grafted_phy_clades_first <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(   phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list, grafting_order = c("clades", "taxa"),   verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # --- Produce several grafted phylogenies --- #  # Each of the 3 simulations grafts both types of missing taxa, with a single seed for both steps grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                               nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) names(grafted_phys) #> [1] "sim_1" "sim_2" "sim_3" attr(grafted_phys, "seeds") #>     sim_1     sim_2     sim_3  #>      1234 488349520 469344150  sapply(grafted_phys, function (x) sum(x$grafted_tips)) #> sim_1 sim_2 sim_3  #>     6     6     6   # --- Account for unsampled species --- #  # Provide the total richness of the clades of both types of taxa # to account for unsampled species (not in the backbone, nor grafted) total_richness_per_clades <- list(   taxa = list(Target_clade = list(c("t26", "t18"), c("t8", "t22"), "t5"),               total_richness = c(30, 25, 4)),   clades = list(Sister_clade = list(c("t8", "t22"), c("t26", "t18")),                 total_richness = c(25, NA)))  # Graft while accounting for unsampled species # (Modify the sampling fractions used during fitting) grafted_phy_richness <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(   phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,   total_richness_per_clades = total_richness_per_clades, return_BD_model_summary = TRUE,   verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) # Inspect info for birth-death models of both steps extract_BD_model_summary(grafted_phy_richness)[, c("step", "b", "d", "rho")] #>     step         b         d       rho #> 1   taxa 0.4232011 0.3643189 0.5666667 #> 2   taxa 1.2056495 1.1935930 0.5600000 #> 3   taxa 0.9835117 0.9736766 0.5200000 #> 4 clades 1.1469268 1.1354575 0.6000000 #> 5 clades 0.2777746 0.2301469 1.0000000  # --- Use several stochastic maps as constraints --- #  # Load backbone and simmap data(toy_backbone) data(toy_simmap)  # Extract tip states tip_states <- phytools::getStates(toy_simmap, type = "tips")  # Produce multiple simmaps conditioned to the tip states set.seed(118) toy_multiSimmap <- phytools::make.simmap(toy_backbone, tip_states,                                          model = "ER", nsim = 2, message = FALSE)  # Build shared missing_taxa_list toy_missing_list <- list(   taxa = list(Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2"),               Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t26", "t18"))),   clades = list(Taxon_name = c("M1", "M2"),                 Sister_clade = list(M1 = "t14", M2 = "t14")))  # Produce grafted phylogenies using the same maps to constrain both steps # Here, we only allow grafting on "green" portions of branches grafted_phys_maps <- graft_missing_taxa_and_clades(   phy = toy_backbone, missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_list, simmap = toy_multiSimmap,   allowed_states = "green", nb_simulations = 2, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Output: a list with one element per map, each a multiPhylo with the simulations of the map names(grafted_phys_maps) #> [1] "map_1" "map_2" names(grafted_phys_maps$map_2) #> [1] "map_2_sim_1" "map_2_sim_2"

--- Update the grafted tips and branches on a pruned phylogeny --- #  # Prune the phylogeny: drop a grafted tip and a backbone tip pruned_phy <- ape::drop.tip(phy = grafted_phy, tip = c("X2", "t1")) # The elements 'grafted_tips' and 'grafted_edges' are NOT updated by ape::drop.tip(): # they still have their previous lengths, and are not valid anymore length(pruned_phy$grafted_tips) == ape::Ntip(pruned_phy) #> [1] FALSE length(pruned_phy$grafted_edges) == nrow(pruned_phy$edge) #> [1] FALSE  # Update them with identify_grafted(), using the grafted taxa still in the pruned phylogeny # (grafted taxa that are not tips are ignored with a warning) pruned_phy <- identify_grafted(    phy = pruned_phy,    grafted_taxa = intersect(missing_taxa_list$Taxon_name, pruned_phy$tip.label))  # Plot the pruned phylogeny with the updated colors plot(pruned_phy, cex = 0.7,      edge.color = c("black", "red")[pruned_phy$grafted_edges + 1],      tip.color = c("black", "red")[pruned_phy$grafted_tips + 1])   # --- Identify the grafted tips and branches on several phylogenies --- #  # Graft multiple phylogenies at once (nb_simulations > 1) grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                    nb_simulations = 2, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Drop a tip across all grafted phylogenies pruned_phys <- ape::drop.tip(phy = grafted_phys, tip = "X2")  # Updated grafting information of all phylogenies at once pruned_phys <- identify_grafted(    phy = pruned_phys,    grafted_taxa = setdiff(missing_taxa_list$Taxon_name, "X2"))  # Inspect updated information across phylogenies sapply(pruned_phys, function (x) sum(x$grafted_tips)) #> sim_1 sim_2  #>     3     3

title: Plot a grafted phylogeny with the grafted taxa highlighted — plot_grafted
code: # --- Prepare data --- #  # Create a toy backbone phylogeny: ultrametric, with a root age of 50 time units set.seed(1234) phy <- ape::rcoal(n = 30) phy$edge.length <- phy$edge.length / max(ape::node.depth.edgelength(phy)) * 50  # List the missing taxa to graft missing_taxa_list <- list(   Taxon_name = c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"),   Target_clade = list(X1 = c("t26", "t18"), X2 = c("t8", "t22"), X3 = "t5", X4 = c("t26", "t18")))  # --- Plot a grafted phylogeny --- #  grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                   verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # Grafted branches and tips are highlighted in red plot_grafted(grafted_phy, cex = 0.7)   # Highlight only the tips, in green plot_grafted(grafted_phy, which = "tips", color = "limegreen", cex = 0.7)   # --- Plot a grafted phylogeny with its simmap --- #  # Simulate a simmap with three states on the backbone Q <- matrix(0.04, 3, 3, dimnames = list(c("A", "B", "C"), c("A", "B", "C"))) diag(Q) <- -0.08 simmap <- phytools::sim.history(phy, Q, anc = "A", message = FALSE)  # Graft the taxa, updating the simmap grafted_phy_states <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                          simmap = simmap, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)  # The simmap is plotted: grafted branches are dashed, grafted tips are labelled in red plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states, simmap_colors = c(A = "lightblue", B = "orange", C = "grey"),              fsize = 0.7, lwd = 3)   # Plot the phylogeny without its simmap plot_grafted(grafted_phy_states, use_simmap = FALSE, cex = 0.7)   # --- Plot one of several simulations --- #  grafted_phys <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = phy, missing_taxa_list = missing_taxa_list,                                    nb_simulations = 3, verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234) plot_grafted(grafted_phys, index = 2, cex = 0.7, main = "Simulation 2")

text: object classes "simmap" "phylo" (see phytools::make.simmap()), tips, topology branch lengths phylograftR::toy_backbone, additional elements $maps (branch, duration spent range, rootward node tipward node), $mapped.edge (total duration per range branch), $node.states $states (ranges nodes tips).

title: Toy stochastic character map of biogeographic ranges of the toy backbone phylogeny — toy_simmap_ranges
text: Events represented map, syntax BioGeoBEARS. Anagenetic changes (along branches, 12 total): 8 "d" (range expansion, gain one area): 5 "" -> "AB" 3 "B" -> "BC". 4 "e" (range contraction, loss one area): 3 "AB" -> "" 1 "AB" -> "B". Cladogenetic events (29 nodes, range lineage node ranges start two descendant branches): 5 "s" (subset sympatry), (AB) -> (AB), (): one descendant keeps widespread range, starts single area within . events produced grafting functions taxon inherits allowed range smaller range lineage grafted (subset sympatric speciation, see phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()). 1 "v" (vicariance), (AB) -> (), (B): widespread range split two descendants. 13 "y" (narrow sympatry): descendants inherit single-area range lineage, () -> (), (). 10 nodes descendants inherit widespread range (widespread sympatry): (AB) -> (AB), (AB) (BC) -> (BC), (BC) (allowed BAYAREALIKE-type models, DEC).

title: Toy taxonomic tables — toy_taxonomic_tables
text: Tables build missing_taxa_list taxonomic names phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(), consistent phylograftR::toy_backbone. toy_backbone_taxonomic_table gives taxonomy 30 tips backbone, four levels (Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus). groups monophyletic. tips group finest levels (NA), often real data. toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table describes 10 taxa graft. first seven (Type = "taxa") taxa phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list, written taxonomic names: clades, excluded subclades stem settings . last three (Type = "clades") taxa graft sister clades phylograftR::graft_missing_clades(): Genus_a_sp1 Genus_a_sp2 belong new genus sister genus Gen_1, grafted together missing clade, Genus_b_sp1 sister tribe. target sister clades written name group (e.g., "Family_B") level (e.g., "Family", meaning family taxon ). tables also provided .csv files system.file("extdata", package = "phylograftR") (toy_backbone_taxonomic_table.csv toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table.csv). clades named taxonomic groups (e.g., "Family_A"), phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list phylograftR::toy_total_richness_per_clades, lists built taxonomy can used richness list.
